book.title: The Most Important Thing: Uncommon Sense for the Thoughtful Investor
book.author: Howard Marks

beats.narration: Okay, tell me why. Yes, it is intensely difficult to beat the market. That's exactly why simple mechanical formulas and algorithms

storyboard.claim: It is intensely difficult to beat the market, and that is exactly why simple mechanical formulas and algorithms...
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal chain diagram on an empty stage: the station ALGORITHMS (a bolt glyph) draws in on 'algorithms'; the stations before and after it wait as dashed '?'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chunk: the hosts answer 'tell me why' by turning to formulas and algorithms.

causal.action: ultimately fail during periods of stress

beats.narration: ultimately fail during periods of stress because they break. Exactly. Algorithms are entirely based on historical data and predictable correlations.

storyboard.claim: Algorithms ultimately fail during periods of stress because they break; they are entirely based on historical data and predictable correlations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same chain: PERIODS OF STRESS (danger glyph) and THEY BREAK (cross) draw in after ALGORITHMS, then HISTORICAL DATA (clock) at the start; a spark tagged PREDICTABLE CORRELATIONS is born on the data and travels into the algorithm.
storyboard.onScreenText: Historical data / Periods of stress / They break / Predictable correlations
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Keeps the chain and adds its start, the stress and the break.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows what the algorithm runs on and where it ends: built on the past, broken by stress.

causal.quote: ultimately fail during periods of stress because they break

beats.narration: They are, in a very real sense, the ultimate first level thinkers just operating at light speed. Oh wow, I never thought of it that way.

storyboard.claim: Algorithms are, in a real sense, the ultimate first-level thinkers operating at light speed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same causal chain held unchanged: historical data feeding the algorithm, stress, the break; the middle WHY station still dashed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Holds the chain while the hosts call the algorithm a first-level thinker.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the 'first-level thinker' label is carried by the audio only.

causal.quote: the ultimate first level thinkers just operating at light speed

storyboard.directorNote: kind commentary was wrong: the beat makes a claim (algorithms are the ultimate first-level thinkers), not banter -> kind idea; the kept causal chain stays as its tool

storyboard.concreteVisual: In the office the consensus investor stands smiling and at ease; Howard Marks beside him talks, calm.

beats.narration: about on a cable news show, it is already baked into the price of the stock. Precisely. If everyone knows it, it is no longer an advantage. It's useless.

storyboard.claim: Widely known information is already baked into the price of the stock; if everyone knows it, it is no longer an advantage - it is useless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow on an empty stage: EVERYONE KNOWS IT -> BAKED INTO THE PRICE -> NO LONGER AN ADVANTAGE.
storyboard.onScreenText: Everyone knows it / Baked into the price / No longer an advantage
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question from beat 6 with its mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows why known news is worthless: the price already holds it.

causal.consequence: it is no longer an advantage
causal.quote: If everyone knows it, it is no longer an advantage

storyboard.claim: Informational advantage only exists when you know something the crowd doesn't, or analyze the same information and draw a completely different conclusion, not blinded by the prevailing emotion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: KNOW WHAT THE CROWD DOESN'T | A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT CONCLUSION.

causal.quote: when you know something the crowd doesn't

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the discipline from beats 5-8 and brings in the human under pressure.

beats.narration: cuz the market isn't a math equation. It's a pendulum of human emotion. And to apply this thinking you really have to understand the environment you're operating in.

storyboard.claim: The market isn't a math equation, it's a pendulum of human emotion; to apply this thinking you must understand the environment.

causal.quote: the market isn't a math equation. It's a pendulum of human emotion
